subject: pathology
title: Caspase Cascades, BCL-2 Family Dynamics, and the Apoptosome

steps.tx: The proteolytic dismantling of a cell during apoptosis is executed by a specialized family of intracellular cysteine-dependent aspartate-directed proteases. Known as **caspases**, these enzymes exist as inactive zymogens in resting cells and are sequentially activated through a hierarchical cascade of initiator and executioner proteases.
steps.say: Caspases are cysteine proteases that cleave after aspartate residues in a coordinated enzymatic cascade.

nodes.label: Caspases Synthesized as Inactive Procaspase Zymogens with Prodomains
Initiator Caspases (8, 9, 10) Undergo Autocatalytic Induced-Proximity Dimerization
Active Initiators Proteolytically Cleave Executioner Caspases (3, 6, 7)
Executioners Cleave Nuclear Scaffold Lamin, Cytoskeleton, and ICAD

steps.tx: Initiator caspases possess lengthy amino-terminal prodomains that mediate protein-protein recruitment interactions. In the extrinsic pathway, procaspases-eight and ten use death effector domains to dock with FADD, whereas in the intrinsic pathway, **procaspase-9 uses caspase recruitment domains** to bind the central hub of the apoptosome.
steps.say: Initiator caspase-9 uses its CARD domain to dock with the apoptosome and initiate intrinsic apoptosis.

left.title: Initiator Caspases (Caspases 8, 9, 10)
points: Possess large N-terminal interaction prodomains (DED or CARD)
Activated as homodimers upon assembly onto multimeric platforms
Function exclusively to cleave and activate downstream executioner zymogens
Do not directly digest cellular architectural proteins

right.title: Executioner Caspases (Caspases 3, 6, 7)
points: Possess short prodomains; pre-exist as inactive dimeric zymogens
Activated by cleavage of interdomain linker by initiator caspases
Directly dismantle cellular architecture by digesting hundreds of targets
Caspase-3 is the chief executioner responsible for apoptotic morphology

steps.tx: Executioner caspase-three carries out the final morphological and biochemical changes of apoptosis. Caspase-three cleaves the inhibitor of caspase-activated deoxyribonuclease, freeing **caspase-activated DNase** to translocate into the nucleus and cleave genomic chromatin specifically at internucleosomal linker regions, producing a diagnostic DNA ladder.
steps.say: Caspase-3 cleaves the inhibitor of CAD, unleashing DNA digestion into internucleosomal fragments.

nodes.label: Inactive CAD Deoxyribonuclease Held Tightly Bound by Inhibitor Protein ICAD
Active Executioner Caspase-3 Specifically Cleaves and Inactivates ICAD
Active CAD Translocates into Nucleus and Attaches to Chromatin
Cleaves Internucleosomal Linker DNA Every 180 to 200 Base Pairs

steps.tx: Mitochondrial membrane permeability is tightly governed by the balance between opposing factions of the BCL-2 protein family. Pro-survival guardians including **BCL-2 and BCL-XL** insert into the outer mitochondrial membrane, where they bind and sequester pro-apoptotic proteins to preserve outer membrane integrity and retain cytochrome c.
steps.say: Anti-apoptotic BCL-2 and BCL-XL preserve mitochondrial membrane integrity, keeping cytochrome c inside.

vis.caption: Intrinsic apoptosis at the mitochondrion: cytochrome c release and apoptosome assembly downstream of the BCL-2 family balance, leading to executioner caspase activation. Illustration: StewardMD original.
vis.alt: Liver carcinoma exhibiting neoplastic resistance to intrinsic apoptosis

steps.tx: Opposing BCL-2 are multi-domain pro-apoptotic effector proteins located within the cytoplasm and outer mitochondrial membrane. When activated by cellular stress, **BAX and BAK** undergo conformational activation and oligomerize into high-conductance macromolecular pores within the outer mitochondrial membrane, permitting the escape of cytochrome c into the cytosol.
steps.say: BAX and BAK oligomerize in outer mitochondrial membranes, forming pores that release cytochrome c.

left.title: Anti-Apoptotic Guardians (BCL-2, BCL-XL, MCL-1)
points: Possess four BCL-2 homology domains (BH1 through BH4)
Reside in outer mitochondrial, ER, and nuclear membranes
Maintain low membrane permeability by binding and sequestering BAX/BAK
Overexpressed in follicular lymphoma due to t(14;18) translocation

right.title: Pro-Apoptotic Effectors (BAX, BAK)
points: Possess BH1, BH2, and BH3 domains but lack BH4 domain
BAX resides in cytosol; BAK is integrated in outer mitochondrial membrane
Stress triggers conformational shift, membrane insertion, and oligomerization
Forms multimeric outer membrane pores that release cytochrome c

steps.tx: Sensory proteins containing only the third BCL-2 homology domain act as damage sentinels. Members such as **BIM, PUMA, and NOXA** are transcriptionally induced by p53 in response to DNA damage, directly neutralizing anti-apoptotic BCL-2 and allosterically activating BAX and BAK to initiate outer membrane permeabilization.
steps.say: BH3-only proteins like BIM and PUMA sense stress, neutralize BCL-2, and activate BAX and BAK.

nodes.label: Severe Genotoxic DNA Damage Induces p53 Transcription Factor
p53 Drives Transcription of BH3-Only Sensors PUMA and NOXA
BH3 Peptides Bind Hydrophobic Groove of BCL-2, Displacing BAX
Unleashed BAX and BAK Oligomerize into Mitochondrial Outer Membrane Pores

steps.tx: In the cytosol, released cytochrome c binds apoptotic protease activating factor-one in the presence of deoxyadenosine triphosphate. Seven cytochrome c and Apaf-1 complexes assemble together into a pinwheel-shaped heptameric macromolecular platform designated the **apoptosome**, which recruits and proteolytically cleaves multiple molecules of initiator procaspase-9.
steps.say: Cytochrome c and Apaf-1 form the heptameric apoptosome, recruiting and activating procaspase-9.

vis.caption: The apoptosome: cytochrome c and Apaf-1 assembling after mitochondrial release to activate caspase-9 and the executioner caspase cascade. Illustration: StewardMD original.
vis.alt: Autoimmune immune-complex formation driven by impaired clearance of apoptotic remnants

steps.tx: Spontaneous accidental activation of executioner caspases is prevented by endogenous intracellular brake proteins known as inhibitors of apoptosis. Concurrently released from mitochondria with cytochrome c, **SMAC and DIABLO** bind and neutralize these inhibitors of apoptosis, lifting the brake to permit full execution of the caspase cascade.
steps.say: Mitochondrial SMAC and DIABLO bind and neutralize inhibitors of apoptosis, permitting caspase activation.

nodes.label: X-Linked Inhibitor of Apoptosis (XIAP) Tonically Inhibits Caspases-3 and 9
Mitochondrial Outer Membrane Pores Release SMAC/DIABLO into Cytosol
SMAC/DIABLO Binds BIR Domains of XIAP with High Affinity
XIAP Dissociates, Allowing Caspase-9 and 3 to Execute Unrestricted Apoptosis
